messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I think you need to add this:

scriptdir = np(system.file("extdata/a_scripts", package="BioGeoBEARS"))
plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_object = decj.results, analysis_titletxt = "DEC*+J", plotsplits=FALSE, cornercoords_loc=scriptdir)

...as in the example script. Without "scriptdir" it defaults to a location you don't have.

(This is there for complex reasons involving the fact that I had to use the APE node coordinates function to do certain plotting features, but the APE function is private, so CRAN wouldn't let me access that, so I have to have a separate script for it, which is located in the "extdata" directory of your local installation of BioGeoBEARS, which is found with the "system.file" function referenced above.)

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Simulations interpretation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

I am doing some simulations in BioGeoBEARS, and I write this because I want to make sure I am doing it correctly. This is what I do:

1. Run BioGeoBEARS with my data (phylogeny and locations).

2. Run the function get_Qmat_COOmat_from_res() with the results object from step 1.

3. Run the function simulate_biogeog_history() with my phylogeny and with the elements $Qmat and $COO_weights_columnar that I got in step 2.

4. Run the function areas_list_to_states_list_new() with my areas to see the correspondence between the numerical states in the results and my geographic ranges.

5. The result from step 3 consists of a vector of numbers, the states in each tip and node.
Here I have a question: is the order in the result the same as in the tree when you do tiplabels() and nodelabels()?

So doing that I am simulating one biogeographic history of my data using the empirical parameters.

Do you think this is correct?

Thank you very much!

Hector

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,

I'm running R version 3.5.1 in RStudio, and BioGeoBEARS 1.1. I've double checked and have no other versions of R or BioGeoBEARS installed on my computer (at least as far as I can tell). I've run a few BioGeoBEARs analyses recently and am having a problem with pdf plots. Everything runs fine, but the pdf plots don't seem to stop saving. By which I mean, when I run the plot code for DEC & DEC+J, the pdf doesn't automatically open (Adobe Reader tells me the document is currently in use by another programme). Then I go ahead and run DIVALIKE and DIVALIKE+J, and plot. The plot again doesn't work. Same for BAYAREALIKE. But pdfs are being saved. messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Problem with pdf plots
messages.body_plain:
Hi - I'm out of the office today, but probably the issue is just with closing the writing of the pdf -- the dev.off() command.

Here's an example:

==================
# Look at your phylogeny (plots to a PDF, which avoids issues with multiple graphics in same window):
pdffn = "tree.pdf"
pdf(file=pdffn, width=9, height=12)

tr = read.tree(trfn)
tr
plot(tr)
title("Example Psychotria phylogeny from Ree & Smith (2008)")
axisPhylo() # plots timescale

dev.off()
cmdstr = paste0("open ", pdffn)
system(cmdstr)
==================

...if you accidentally skip those last 3 lines, things can get messed up:

dev.off()  says "stop writing to the PDF file"
the "cmdstr" stuff says "open filename.pdf" to your operating system.

But, if you miss the dev.off(), the PDF stays on "being written", which means it can't be opened or will be corrupted -- if you then go run more graphics or PDF commands, you will get graphics not appearing or corrupt PDFs.

The main solution is:

1. Run "dev.off()" a bunch of times until it is clear all files and graphics objects are closed.

2. Then, re-run the entirety of the pdf block (e.g. like the above code) at once.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi -- this one was a beast to figure out.  It turns out that your phylogeny, somehow, has most of the tips at age

0.07019192 my before present

and some at

0.02674141 my before present

Only 1 tip is actually at 0.00000000 my before present.  Then, you have time-slices at 0.01 and 0.012 my before present, so the time-stratification analysis is trying to slice the tree into two tiny slices on that slightly-longer tip branch, resulting in trees with 1 tip, resulting in this error:

============
Error in current_tip_relative_probs_of_each_state[tip_TF, states_to_use_TF] :
  (subscript) logical subscript too long
============

...which is the real error, only further down giving:

===========
Error in bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object) :

  STOP ERROR #3 in bears_optim_run(). Test calculation of the likelihood with calc_loglike_for_optim_stratified() returned LnL=-1e+50, which is not a valid starting likelihood. Probably, you have an overly constrained analysis and have thus made your data impossible. For example, if your tips had ranges A and B, but you disallowed the state AB, then your data would be impossible under DEC, because AB is a required intermediate state. Try removing some of the areas allowed/area adjacency/manual states list constraints.  You can also try changing manual dispersal multipliers from 0 to some small value (e.g. 0.00001) -- note that this can works on dispersal multiplers, but NOT on area constraints, which have to be 0 or 1.  Have a CAREFUL THINK about what you are doing and why you think the list of ranges should be so constrained - do you actually have a good argument for your constraints?

===========

...which is BioGeoBEARS's response when the try() function calculating the likelihood fails to produce a real number.

You can see this feature of your tree with:

trtable = prt(tr, printflag=FALSE)
trtable

...looking at trtable$time_bp.  Presumably you don't have dozens of fossil tips with the same age, and only 1 living species, so the problem is with your tree.

It would be nice to have an error trap for this, but sometimes people have real fossils with tip ages older than 0.0, so it's complex.

SOLUTIONS:

A. I got it to run by changing:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE)
to:
BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE, cut_fossils=FALSE, fossils_older_than=0.0001)

...but this treats all those tips as fossils.

B. Would be to fix your tree, either by fixing whatever analysis gave you that tree, or by editing the Newick file to add/subtract the necessary amounts to make all the tip branches come to 0.0000

C. Remove the tiny timeslices from the top of your timeperiods file, I imagine you are trying to do something with Holocene / end-ice-age connectivity, this may be irrelevant at the very coarse timescale covered by a phylogeny spanning 45 Ma.

I recommend Option B, plus having a hard think about (C) whether a phylogenetic biogeography analysis spanning 10s of millions of years can realistically detect much about the last 12,000 years.

OTHER ISSUES:

A. Units of distance are arbitrary, so we recommend dividing by the minimum distance so that the closest distance has a relative distance of 1, other distances are relative to that.  Actual connectivity (0 distance) should be specified by a dispersal multiplier matrix.

B. And, you should turn on the +x model if you are using distance, e.g. add this to each model:

===============
# Add x as a free parameter
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["x","type"] = "free"
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["x","init"] = 0.0
BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table["x","est"] = 0.0
===============

Cheers,
Nick
